props.name: error
props.description: The validation message. Its presence drives `aria-invalid`.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the field invalid independently of whether `error` is set.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name, and the label rendered above the field.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder. Never a substitute for a label.

ai.summary: A text field with a filterable list of options — type to narrow, arrows to choose.
whenToUse: There are more options than fit in a Select — roughly more than fifteen
The reader may know part of the name and want to type it
Options have labels the reader searches by, not just values
whenNotToUse: There are fewer than about eight options — use a Radio Group or Select
Free text is a valid answer — use an Input
Multiple selections are needed — use a multi-select pattern instead
ai.accessibility: The ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern: the input carries `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` naming the listbox, and **focus never leaves the input** — the active option is reported through `aria-activedescendant` instead. Moving focus into the list is the common mistake: it blurs the field the reader is typing into and every screen reader announces it as leaving. Arrows wrap rather than dead-ending. Escape closes without clearing the typed text, because closing is not the same command as reverting. `sk-value-change` fires only for a committed selection — typing filters and is not a value change (§4).
knownLimitations: Matching is a plain case-insensitive substring — the wrong collation for some locales, and §6 leaves locale to the consumer, who may pass pre-filtered options
No `aria-live` result count: it interrupts on every keystroke, and the listbox relationship already conveys the change
SSR consumers must pass an explicit id — the counter differs between server and client
